transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having some thoughts I don’t really like to admit. Nothing I’m proud of. I keep thinking maybe my family would be better off if I just… didn’t wake up. And that scared me enough that I finally told my supervisor.
Did something stressful happen in your life before these thoughts started?

Yeah… I think so. It’s been about two weeks now, since my daughter left Georgia for the military. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t handle things, but that’s when I started feeling like this whole change in me really began.
Do these thoughts and low mood seem mainly tied to your daughter leaving for the military?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to put it all on that, but that’s really when I noticed the change. Since she left Georgia for the military, it’s been about two weeks of me feeling this way. I guess that lines up, if that makes sense.
Since this started, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I guess I have, some. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but things I’d usually enjoy just don’t pull me in right now. I used to mess with my tomato plants, sand wood out at my bench, watch the Falcons, stay after church and talk with folks… lately I just kind of look at all that like it belongs to somebody else, if that makes sense.
How has your sleep been since this started?

I’m not real sure how to answer that. I mean… I’ve been sleeping, I guess, but I haven’t really been keeping track of it or anything. It may be a little off, but I don’t want to say more than I know. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Before your daughter left, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed like this for days or weeks at a time?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t know that I would’ve called it depressed, maybe just “in a low spell” or not quite myself. Looking back, it’s been happening off and on for maybe about a year now… stretches where I’d feel down for days, sometimes longer. But this one since my daughter left, this has felt the hardest, if that answers what you’re asking.
Before your daughter left, was there ever a time when feeling down lasted for two weeks or longer?

I think… yeah, probably. I don’t want to overstate it, but looking back those low stretches have been showing up off and on for about a year. Some of them may have run a couple weeks, maybe longer. This time after my daughter left is the one that’s hit me the hardest, though.
Before your daughter left, did you ever have a stretch of feeling down nearly every day for two weeks or longer?

I think so, yes… looking back, those low stretches have been coming around for about a year now. I maybe didn’t pay close attention to whether it was every single day, but there were times it felt pretty steady for a couple weeks or more. This one after my daughter left has definitely hit me the hardest, though.
Before your daughter left, during those earlier low stretches, did you ever have thoughts that you’d be better off dead or not wake up?

I… yeah. I mean, I don’t like saying that out loud. It wasn’t like I had some big plan or anything, but I did keep having these thoughts that maybe my family would be better off if I just didn’t wake up. That’s actually part of why I came in… it scared me enough that I told my supervisor. Is that… is that the kind of thing you mean?
Between those earlier low periods and this current one, was there ever a time when you felt back to your usual self for at least two months?

I’m not really sure, to be honest. I’d like to say I bounced back completely, but I don’t know if it was for a full two months. There were times I was doing better and kind of getting through things normally, but whether that was my “usual self” for that long… I’m not sure. Does that make sense?
Between those earlier low periods and this current one, was there ever a stretch of at least two months when you felt back to your usual self?

I honestly don’t know if I can say that for sure. There were stretches where I was doing better and trying to act normal, you know, keeping up with things. But a full two months of feeling really like myself… I’m not sure. I don’t want to give you the wrong answer.
If your daughter hadn’t left for the military, do you think you would still be feeling this depressed right now?

I don’t know… I mean, her leaving definitely hit me hard, so part of me wants to say maybe I’d be doing better. But I can’t honestly say I’d be completely fine if she hadn’t gone. I’ve had low times before, so… I’m not sure how to separate it. Is that a fair answer?
Since your daughter left, has how depressed you feel seemed stronger than you would expect from that change alone?

I’m not sure. I mean, it feels heavy, but I also don’t know what’s “normal” for something like that, you know? I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. It just… affected me a lot, but whether it’s more than you’d expect, I can’t really say.
Before this current depression started, was there ever a stretch of at least two months when you felt completely back to your usual self?

I’m not really sure, doctor. I had times where I was functioning better and probably looked more like myself to people, but “completely back” for two whole months… I can’t say that with confidence. I don’t want to overstate it either way.
Before your daughter left, did you ever have a period when the depression had clearly lifted before it came back again?

I don’t think it ever clearly lifted, not in a way I could point to and say, “Okay, I’m back to normal now.” Looking back, these low stretches have kind of been coming around for maybe about a year… but this one after my daughter left, that’s the one that’s hit me the hardest. Does that make sense?
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energized or high, much more than your normal self?

Yeah… I guess there have been times before this low spell where I felt, uh, more fired up than usual. Like things were finally going my way and I had more energy than I normally do.

I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but sometimes it was more like I’d get wound up, or I’d snap at people over little things I’d usually let go. Does that count as what you mean?
During those times when you felt more fired up than usual, did you need much less sleep than normal?

I’m not sure I’d say I needed much less sleep, exactly. I might’ve stayed up a little later here and there, but I don’t remember it being like I could go on hardly any sleep and feel fine. I don’t want to answer that wrong—sleep’s a little hard for me to pin down looking back.
During those times when you felt more fired up than usual, did you feel unusually confident or like you could do things other people couldn’t?

Maybe a little, yeah. I mean, I don’t want it to sound like I thought I was some genius or anything… but I did get it in my head that I was about to be regional director, and that nobody in the company really understood operations the way I did.

That’s not usually how I talk about myself, so… looking back, it was probably more than normal confidence. Does that answer what you mean?
During those times when you felt more fired up than usual, did you start taking on a lot more projects or activities than was normal for you?

Yeah… I mean, I probably did. I didn’t think of it as a problem at the time. It felt more like I was just being productive, you know?

I’d be up before daylight planning changes at the warehouse, thinking through how things should be set up, and then I’d come home and start cleaning out the garage or jumping into some other job. I was kind of going from one thing to the next and didn’t really want to stop.

Maybe that’s more than normal. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you’re asking about.
When you had those more fired-up periods, did they last at least four days in a row?

I’m not sure I can say that for certain. It wasn’t like I was marking it on a calendar, you know?

Some of those stretches felt like they went on a few days, maybe longer, but I’d be guessing if I said yes to four days straight. I don’t want to overstate it. Is it okay to say I’m not sure?
